item.title: Google Says Go Is the Ideal Language for AI Coding — HN Argues Back in 317 Comments
item.description: Google's developer blog called Go the ideal language for AI-assisted engineering; Hacker News answered with 317 comments. Our take: both sides are doing the wrong math. In the AI era you pick a language by verification cost, not writing speed — here is the three-factor ledger, our picks, and an experiment to run tonight

item.title: Go 2026 Survival Guide for Backend Engineers: The Changes That Actually Affect Production
item.description: Go 1.25 and 1.26 bring container-aware GOMAXPROCS, go fix overhaul, Green Tea GC, testing/synctest, and more. A practical breakdown of what backend engineers actually need to know.

item.title: Go Memory Allocator: A Warehouse Manager's Tale
item.description: From 64MB warehouses to 8KB shelves, discover how Go's three-level cache architecture makes memory allocation blazing fast. Deep dive into arena, span, and size class design philosophy.

item.title: Go + sqlc + Postgres: The Zero-ORM Stack Behind Cloudflare's 99.99% Uptime
item.description: Cloudflare runs Go + sqlc + Postgres in production, bypassing GORM's N+1 queries and reflection overhead. 85K vs 42K qps, p99 drops from 3.8ms to 1.2ms. Breaking down the design logic, migration patterns, and when it actually makes sense to switch.

item.title: Go 1.26 Shipped Without JSON v2: 18 of 44 Tasks Still Open
item.description: Go 1.26 is out, but JSON v2 remains experimental. With 18 of 44 subtasks still open, unresolved performance regressions, and pending Union type support—this isn't a delay, it's the Go team building a solid foundation for the standard library.

item.title: Go to Rust Axum Migration: Lessons and Savings
item.description: This isn't a story about flexing how fast Rust is. It's about how tech choices translate to real money, and why most rewrite projects can't replicate this result.

item.title: 10x Performance Boost Secret: 99% Don't Know These Go Concurrent GC Tricks
item.description: Production latency dropped from 500ms to 50ms! Deep dive into Go's tri-color marking algorithm, write barriers, and GOGC tuning. Say goodbye to lag forever.
